newsitem.title: UK: IPE natural gas slides again as trade volume grows.
newsitem.headline: IPE natural gas slides again as trade volume grows.

text.p: The IPE natural gas contract continued to fall on Tuesday afternoon, tracking physical prices downwards.

By the close, 280 lots had traded, representing a little over 8,500,000 therms in total. This compared with 465 lots on Friday, the contract's first day, and a mere 40 lots on Monday when the contract was beset by controversy over a "busted" trade and by a computer problem.

March fell by 1.195 pence a therm to hit a contract low of 12.000 pence, and Feb 1998 fell by 1.790 pence, although the February market was much thinner. Trade was seen in seven of the 12 forward months on the contract
"We're very, very pleased with the increased volume," said a futures broker, adding that one of their clients had traded 110 of the 280 lots through his firm.

He added that one development noticed on the market on Tuesday afternoon was that players were not being so quick to close out their positions on the day, leading to greater open interest and creating more of a true futures market.

"It's just what the market needs," he said, adding that there was a reasonable bid/offer spread across most periods and that "most people will be a lot happier" with the extra volume done after the thin trade on Monday.

Prices on futures and physical markets have fallen sharply since the contract opened. But futures brokers are so far unwilling to offer an explanation for price movements on the futures markets, allowing themselves to be led in terms of price by traders on the physical market.
